messages:
lee: heads up — the nightly DAST run in staging produced a huge spike of findings this morning, most are 404/403 authenticated endpoints flagged as vuln because scanner is using ephemeral creds that hit KMS-authenticated endpoints :grimace:
maria: ugh, saw that. looks like the scanner service account doesn't have the same RBAC as prod so it triggers a bunch of false positives. also no audit-proof linking the scan request to a KMS audit entry yet.
aj: can you paste an example finding? is it all the same endpoint or different paths?
lee: same endpoint pattern: /internal/* (auth required). scanner tries to sign a session token, KMS returns temporary creds, but the scanner retries with 401 and DAST marks it as potential auth bypass. short snippet of the raw scanner log:
```
[2026-03-19T02:10:12Z] scan-request id=abcd1234 target=/internal/config  -> 401, retry -> signed by kms-key=scanner-ephemeral, signed-token=ey..
[2026-03-19T02:10:12Z] result=potential-auth-bypass confidence=medium
```
lee: security-bot posted the run summary: (attached) 72 findings, 56 likely false positives.
security-bot: automated: DAST run 2301234500 completed. findings=72, high=3, medium=21, low=48. link: https://circle/scans/2301234500 :robot_face:
maria: couple things we should do: 1) make scanner use a scanner-specific RBAC role that only can call KMS Sign/Encrypt but not access secrets; 2) attach an audit-proof id to the scan request that we can correlate with KMS audit logs (request-id header); 3) add scanner evidence blob with a KMS signature so triage can verify authenticity.
aj: agree. also for staging we can add a pre-filter: if scanner gets 401->signed-token flow, mark as authenticated-flow and don't surface as vuln unless follow-up suspicious behavior detected.
sam: oncall here — want to avoid noisy pages. can we gate the devex webhook that sends high findings? temporarily throttle notifications for staging scans until we reduce noise.
maria: yes, throttle devex webhook for channel #security-staging-alerts. also create suppression rules in the scanner config for endpoints under /internal/ when authenticated flow present. we'll require a signed evidence artifact for any suppression to be accepted in triage.
lee: what's the plan for the audit-proof id? I can implement header injection in the scanner 
(missed by default). idea: scanner includes `X-Scan-Trace: scan-<scan-id>` and we ensure KMS logs include that trace via request metadata.
aj: for AWS KMS we can use the `GrantTokens`/`EncryptionContext` fields to pass a trace id: e.g., `EncryptionContext={"scan-id":"scan-2301234500"}`. then correlate CloudTrail events by that context key.
maria: perfect — add that to the scanner runtime. also create a lightweight proof format: JSON file with {scan_id, target, timestamp, sig} where `sig` = KMS-sign(sha256(evidence)). example command to sign locally for dev testing:
```
echo -n '{"scan_id":"scan-2301234500","target":"/internal/config","ts":"2026-03-19T02:10:12Z"}' > evidence.json
# sign with KMS (example)
aws kms sign --key-id alias/scanner-signer --message fileb://evidence.json --message-type RAW --signing-algorithm RSASSA_PKCS1_V1_5_SHA_256 --output text > signature.bin
base64 signature.bin > signature.b64
```
lee: that'll make triage quicker; reviewers can drop the evidence blob into a quick verifier script to confirm KMS signed it.
sam: for RBAC changes, who's owning policy updates? we need a PR and security review.
maria: i'll own the policy PR (sec infra). target: update the scanner service account policy to only allow `kms:Sign`, `kms:Encrypt` with conditions limiting key usage to `scanner/*` and enforce `aws:RequestTag/scan-id` presence. i'll open a PR and request eng-sre and infra review.
aj: i'll review once you open it. also we should update pre-merge CI so that any PR changing scanner RBAC requires a security-ok label.
lee: created ticket: PROC-5678, summary: "DAST false positive reduction — scanner RBAC + evidence signing + notification throttling". cc @maria @aj @sam
maria: added checklist to ticket: (1) implement EncryptionContext/trace id, (2) KMS-signed evidence artifact, (3) scanner suppression rules, (4) webhook throttling, (5) update premerge gate for RBAC PRs.
security-bot: note: created PROC-5678 and linked to repo: https://git/repo/PR/1423 :robot_face: :white_check_mark:
lee: timeline? can we do a hotfix for throttling + suppression rules today?
aj: suppression rules + webhook throttle can be rolled in a single small deploy. I can do a canary to staging later today.
sam: i'll standby for any pages, ping me once throttle is live.
maria: will draft PR tonight, aiming for merge tomorrow. I'll add acceptance tests that verify `EncryptionContext` header present in KMS calls and that CloudTrail entries include `scan-id`.
lee: cool. for triage notes, we'll add a column in the ticket for "audit-proof link" that points to signed evidence blob. triage playbook will require that for suppressions.
aj: small nit — ensure that suppressions are per-scan, expiring after 7 days unless re-justified, to avoid permanent masks.
maria: agreed. expiring suppressions by default = 7 days, extension requires security-owner sign-off.
lee: thanks everyone. I'll watch the canary and report false-positive count change. :eyes:
maria: thanks — threading into the compliance backlog for the KMS audit proof requirement.
security-bot: reminder: next security-triage sync Wed 14:00 UTC to verify suppression impact and triage metrics.
lee: ack. end of thread.
